title: AI and the Future of Academic Peer Review

bias_targets.methodology: Literature review synthesizing existing empirical studies that analyze acceptance rates and reviewer preferences (both human and LLM) for male versus female authors.
Reviewing large-scale experiments and empirical data that vary author prominence and university affiliation to measure favoritism in peer review evaluations.
Evaluating literature on the systemic disadvantages faced by non-native English speakers in manuscript ratings, and analyzing the risk of LLM-driven linguistic homogenization.
Conceptual analysis of LLMs' limitations in assessing non-Western scholarly traditions (e.g., Ubuntu philosophy, Buddhist logic) due to disparities in training data representation.
Assessing the tendency of RLHF-aligned LLMs and human reviewers to favor established paradigms and conventional ideas over paradigm-shifting, innovative research.
